2. SUBSTANTIVE ANALYSIS (Article 238): Dealt with former princely state unions governed by Rajpramukhs. Formally repealed and deleted by the 7th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1956. Applying the governing principle—'Ended the special status of Rajpramukhs and transitional princely covenants.'—the impugned constitutional reference / proclamation by the Legislative Secretariat / Presiding Officer must strictly satisfy constitutional bounds.

3. PRECEDENT (Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973)) & RELIEF: Guided by Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973), any overreach inconsistent with Article 238 is liable to be quashed or suitably restrained.
